claim: Intracortical inhibition plays a critical role in shaping activity patterns in the mature cortex.
source: Intracortical inhibition plays a critical role in shaping activity patterns in the mature cortex.
evidence: This is a general statement about the role of inhibition in mature cortex, drawing from established scientific understanding.

claim: Little is known about the structure of inhibition in early development prior to the onset of sensory experience.
source: However, little is known about the structure of inhibition in early development prior to the onset of sensory experience, a time when spontaneous activity exhibits long-range correlations predictive of mature functional networks.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Spontaneous activity exhibits long-range correlations predictive of mature functional networks during early development prior to sensory experience.
source: However, little is known about the structure of inhibition in early development prior to the onset of sensory experience, a time when spontaneous activity exhibits long-range correlations predictive of mature functional networks.
evidence: This refers to prior findings about spontaneous activity patterns in early development.

claim: Spontaneous activity in inhibitory neurons is highly organized into distributed modular networks before visual experience in ferret visual cortex.
source: Here, using calcium imaging of GABAergic neurons in the ferret visual cortex, we show that spontaneous activity in inhibitory neurons is already highly organized into distributed modular networks before visual experience.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by calcium imaging data.

claim: Inhibitory neurons exhibit spatially modular activity with long-range correlations in developing ferret visual cortex.
source: Inhibitory neurons exhibit spatially modular activity with long-range correlations and precise local organization that is in quantitative agreement with excitatory networks.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by correlation analysis of calcium imaging data.

claim: Inhibitory networks exhibit precise local organization that is in quantitative agreement with excitatory networks.
source: Inhibitory neurons exhibit spatially modular activity with long-range correlations and precise local organization that is in quantitative agreement with excitatory networks.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative comparison of inhibitory and excitatory network properties.

claim: Excitatory and inhibitory networks are strongly co-aligned at both millimeter and cellular scales.
source: Furthermore, excitatory and inhibitory networks are strongly co-aligned at both millimeter and cellular scales.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by widefield and two-photon imaging data.

claim: GABAergic interneurons have been implicated in response gain, stimulus discrimination, and network stabilization.
source: GABAergic interneurons have been implicated in a range of computations, including response gain, stimulus discrimination, and network stabilization (for reviews, see Isaacson and Scanziani, 2011; Denève and Machens, 2016; Ferguson and Cardin, 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: In the columnar visual cortex, inhibitory neurons actively shape response selectivity.
source: In the columnar visual cortex, inhibitory neurons actively shape response selectivity (Wilson et al., 2018) and are organized into functionally-specific networks with excitatory neurons (Wilson et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wilson et al., 2018.

claim: Inhibitory neurons are organized into functionally-specific networks with excitatory neurons in the columnar visual cortex.
source: In the columnar visual cortex, inhibitory neurons actively shape response selectivity (Wilson et al., 2018) and are organized into functionally-specific networks with excitatory neurons (Wilson et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wilson et al., 2017.

claim: GABAergic inhibition is initially absent in early development before progressively strengthening as the cortex matures.
source: GABAergic inhibition is initially absent in early development before progressively strengthening as the cortex matures (reviewed in Ben-Ari, 2002; Huang et al., 2007), raising the possibility that inhibition plays only a minor role in shaping early patterns of cortical activity.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Prior to the onset of visual experience in ferret visual cortex, excitatory activity is already highly structured, showing modular and distributed activity with long-range correlations.
source: Recent work in the ferret visual cortex demonstrated that prior to the onset of visual experience, excitatory activity is already highly structured, showing modular and distributed activity with long-range correlations (Smith et al., 2018), reminiscent of the columnar stimulus-evoked activity found in the mature cortex (Hubel and Wiesel, 1968; Blasdel and Salama, 1986; Weliky et al., 1996; Issa et al., 2000; Kara and Boyd, 2009; Smith et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Smith et al., 2018.

claim: Early excitatory activity patterns are reminiscent of the columnar stimulus-evoked activity found in the mature cortex.
source: Recent work in the ferret visual cortex demonstrated that prior to the onset of visual experience, excitatory activity is already highly structured, showing modular and distributed activity with long-range correlations (Smith et al., 2018), reminiscent of the columnar stimulus-evoked activity found in the mature cortex (Hubel and Wiesel, 1968; Blasdel and Salama, 1986; Weliky et al., 1996; Issa et al., 2000; Kara and Boyd, 2009; Smith et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to studies of mature cortex.

claim: Correlated networks in developing ferret visual cortex are not abolished when silencing feedforward activity.
source: These correlated networks are not abolished when silencing feedforward activity and predict future visually-evoked responses (Smith et al., 2018), suggesting a key role for early spontaneous activity in the development of mature cortical networks.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Smith et al., 2018.

claim: Correlated networks in developing ferret visual cortex predict future visually-evoked responses.
source: These correlated networks are not abolished when silencing feedforward activity and predict future visually-evoked responses (Smith et al., 2018), suggesting a key role for early spontaneous activity in the development of mature cortical networks.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Smith et al., 2018.

claim: GABAergic signaling switches from exerting depolarizing effects to hyperpolarizing due to the maturation of intracellular chloride concentrations over the course of development.
source: Over the course of development, GABAergic signaling switches from exerting depolarizing effects to hyperpolarizing due to the maturation of intracellular chloride concentrations (Ben-Ari, 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Ben-Ari, 2002.

claim: Functional GABAergic synapses have been shown to be present as early as postnatal day 20 (P20) in ferret.
source: In the ferret, functional GABAergic synapses have been shown to be present as early as postnatal day 20 (P20) (Dalva, 2010), but because these experiments utilized whole-cell recordings in cortical slices, it remains unclear whether these synapses exert an inhibitory effect at this age.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Dalva, 2010.

claim: BMI resulted in a pronounced increase in the frequency of spontaneous events in excitatory neurons at P21-23.
source: BMI resulted in a pronounced increase in the frequency (Figure 2c; p<0.001; baseline=0.030 [0.016–0.050] Hz; BMI=0.200 [0.129–0.271] Hz, n=4 animals; median, interquartile range [IQR], Wilcoxon rank-sum test) and amplitude of spontaneous events
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from BMI application experiments shown in Figure 2c.

claim: BMI resulted in a pronounced increase in the amplitude of spontaneous events in excitatory neurons at P21-23.
source: BMI resulted in a pronounced increase in the frequency (Figure 2c; p<0.001; baseline=0.030 [0.016–0.050] Hz; BMI=0.200 [0.129–0.271] Hz, n=4 animals; median, interquartile range [IQR], Wilcoxon rank-sum test) and amplitude of spontaneous events (Figure 2d; p<0.001; baseline=0.374 [0.190–0.535] ∆F/F, n [across four animals]=274 events; BMI=0.974 [0.470–1.220] ∆F/F, n=732 events; median, IQR, Wilcoxon rank-sum test)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from BMI application experiments shown in Figure 2d.

claim: In vivo GABA exerts a strong net inhibitory action at P21-23 in ferret visual cortex.
source: BMI resulted in a pronounced increase in the frequency (Figure 2c; p<0.001; baseline=0.030 [0.016–0.050] Hz; BMI=0.200 [0.129–0.271] Hz, n=4 animals; median, interquartile range [IQR], Wilcoxon rank-sum test) and amplitude of spontaneous events (Figure 2d; p<0.001; baseline=0.374 [0.190–0.535] ∆F/F, n [across four animals]=274 events; BMI=0.974 [0.470–1.220] ∆F/F, n=732 events; median, IQR, Wilcoxon rank-sum test), demonstrating that in vivo GABA exerts a strong net inhibitory action at this point of development.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the BMI disinhibition experiments.

claim: The mDlx enhancer drives expression specifically in GABAergic cells.
source: To examine the structure of inhibitory networks in early development, we performed a series of experiments in which GABAergic neurons were specifically labeled via virally mediated expression of GCaMP6s under control of the mDlx enhancer, which was previously shown to drive expression specifically in GABAergic cells (Dimidschstein et al., 2016; Wilson et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Dimidschstein et al., 2016 and Wilson et al., 2017.

claim: Inhibitory neuron populations showed frequent spontaneous activity that exhibited a highly modular structure at P23-29.
source: Under light anesthesia, inhibitory neuron populations showed frequent spontaneous activity that exhibited a highly modular structure, with spontaneous events containing multiple distinct domains of activity distributed across the imaging field-of-view (FOV) and spanning several millimeters (Figure 3b–c, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by widefield imaging data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Inhibitory neurons exhibit a spatially extended correlation structure with both strong positively and negatively correlated domains extending several millimeters from the reference seed point.
source: We found that inhibitory neurons indeed exhibit a spatially extended correlation structure, with both strong positively and negatively correlated domains extending several millimeters from the reference seed point (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Peak values of positively correlated domains in inhibitory networks were statistically significant up to 2 mm away from the seed point.
source: Peak values of positively correlated domains were statistically significant up to 2 mm away from the seed point (Figure 3e; p<0.01 vs. surrogate data, 6 of 7 individual animals, bootstrap test), demonstrating the large-scale nature of inhibitory networks in the developing visual cortex.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of correlation data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: Orientation preference maps in mature cortex exhibit smooth variation, punctuated by abrupt discontinuities at orientation pinwheels and fractures.
source: In the mature cortex, orientation preference maps exhibit smooth variation, punctuated by abrupt discontinuities at orientation pinwheels and fractures (Bonhoeffer and Grinvald, 1991; Ohki et al., 2005), an organization shared by inhibitory neurons in the mature ferret (Wilson et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to studies of mature cortex.

claim: Inhibitory neurons in mature ferret share the organization of orientation preference maps with smooth variation and abrupt discontinuities.
source: In the mature cortex, orientation preference maps exhibit smooth variation, punctuated by abrupt discontinuities at orientation pinwheels and fractures (Bonhoeffer and Grinvald, 1991; Ohki et al., 2005), an organization shared by inhibitory neurons in the mature ferret (Wilson et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wilson et al., 2017.

claim: Prior work identified similar discontinuities (correlation fractures) in the patterns of distributed correlated activity in excitatory neurons early in development prior to the emergence of orientation maps.
source: Notably, prior work identified similar discontinuities in the patterns of distributed correlated activity (termed correlation fractures) in excitatory neurons early in development prior to the emergence of orientation maps (Smith et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Smith et al., 2018.

claim: Developing inhibitory networks exhibit spatially discrete fractures over which inhibitory correlation patterns exhibit abrupt changes in structure.
source: This analysis revealed the presence of spatially discrete fractures over which inhibitory correlation patterns exhibit abrupt changes in structure, demonstrating a precise local organization in the coupling to large-scale inhibitory networks in the developing primary visual cortex (Figure 3f).
evidence: This is supported by fracture analysis shown in Figure 3f.

claim: Domain size was similar between inhibitory and excitatory events.
source: Domain size was similar between inhibitory and excitatory events (Figure 4a; minor axis: I: 412.06 μm [386.73–439.94], n=7 animals; E: 392.68 μm [371.46–397.49], n=7 animals; median [IQR]; p = 0.142, Wilcoxon rank-sum test)
evidence: This is supported by quantitative comparison of domain sizes shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Correlations were similarly long-range between excitatory and inhibitory networks, with equivalent strength 2 mm away from the seed point.
source: We find that correlations were similarly long-range, with equivalent strength 2 mm away from the seed point (Figure 4c; I: r=0.29 (0.25–0.31), E: r=0.24 [0.27–0.31]; p=0.848, Wilcoxon rank-sum test).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4c.

claim: The wavelength estimated from the full angle-averaged correlation function was similar between inhibitory and excitatory networks.
source: Likewise, the wavelength estimated from the full angle-averaged correlation function was similar between inhibitory and excitatory networks (Figure 4d,e; I: 0.84 mm [0.70–0.96], E: 0.81 mm [0.77–0.901]; p=0.848, Wilcoxon rank-sum test)
evidence: This is supported by wavelength analysis shown in Figure 4d,e.

claim: The wavelength of inhibitory and excitatory networks is approximately similar to the wavelength of orientation columns in the mature cortex.
source: Likewise, the wavelength estimated from the full angle-averaged correlation function was similar between inhibitory and excitatory networks (Figure 4d,e; I: 0.84 mm [0.70–0.96], E: 0.81 mm [0.77–0.901]; p=0.848, Wilcoxon rank-sum test), and approximately similar to the wavelength of orientation columns in the mature cortex (Bonhoeffer and Grinvald, 1993; White et al., 2001b; Kaschube et al., 2010).
evidence: This comparison is supported by citations to studies of mature cortex.

claim: Correlations in inhibitory networks exhibited a strong local anisotropy, with local correlations around the seed point showing a high degree of eccentricity that was consistent with excitatory correlations.
source: Additionally, correlations in inhibitory networks exhibited a strong local anisotropy, with local correlations around the seed point showing a high degree of eccentricity that was consistent with excitatory correlations (Figure 4f,g; I: 0.70 [0.66–0.73], E: 0.69 [0.67–0.71]; p=0.949, Wilcoxon rank-sum test).
evidence: This is supported by eccentricity analysis shown in Figure 4f,g.

claim: The strength of correlation fractures was highly similar between excitatory and inhibitory networks.
source: Finally, we found that the strength of correlation fractures was highly similar between excitatory and inhibitory networks, reflecting a similar degree of precision in fine-scale network organization (Figure 4h; I: 1.86*10–3 (per μm) [1.49*10–3 –2.13*10–3], E: 1.62*10–3 (per μm)[1.35*10–3–2.22*10–3]; p=0.655, Wilcoxon rank-sum test).
evidence: This is supported by fracture strength analysis shown in Figure 4h.

claim: In locally heterogeneous network models that recapitulate the structure of developing excitatory networks, long-range correlations exhibiting both local anisotropy and pronounced fractures strongly coincide with spontaneous activity patterns that reside in a low-dimensional subspace.
source: Prior work has shown that in locally heterogeneous network models that recapitulate the structure of developing excitatory networks, long-range correlations exhibiting both local anisotropy and pronounced fractures strongly coincide with spontaneous activity patterns that reside in a low-dimensional subspace (Smith et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Smith et al., 2018.

claim: Across animals, inhibitory and excitatory events tended to reside in similarly low-dimensional subspaces.
source: We found that across animals, inhibitory and excitatory events tended to reside in similarly low-dimensional subspaces (Figure 4i,j; I: 10.55 [9.60–11.78], E: 9.44 [8.44–10.01]; median [IQR]; p=0.142, Wilcoxon rank-sum test)
evidence: This is supported by dimensionality analysis shown in Figure 4i,j.

claim: When selecting the same seed point, the spatial patterns of correlated activity were highly similar across excitatory and inhibitory networks.
source: When selecting the same seed point, the spatial patterns of correlated activity were highly similar across networks (Figure 5b), and exhibited equivalent strength extending across several millimeters (Figure 5e).
evidence: This is supported by correlation pattern comparison shown in Figure 5b.

claim: Excitatory and inhibitory correlation similarity is significantly greater than surrogate.
source: We find that excitatory and inhibitory correlation similarity is significantly greater than surrogate (p<0.01 for 3 of 3 individual animals, bootstrap test) and near the level of within inhibitory similarity (Figure 5d and f; colors correspond to data from three individual animals).
evidence: This is supported by statistical comparison shown in Figure 5d and f.

claim: Excitatory and inhibitory networks exhibit strong similarity even in their long-range correlations, as similarity remained significantly greater than surrogate even when considering only correlations over 1.4 mm from the seed point.
source: Notably, excitatory and inhibitory networks exhibit strong similarity even in their long-range correlations, as similarity remained significantly greater than surrogate even when considering only correlations over 1.4 mm from the seed point (Figure 5g; p<0.01, I vs. E networks vs surrogate, bootstrap test).
evidence: This is supported by long-range correlation analysis shown in Figure 5g.

claim: Local populations of excitatory and inhibitory cells show tightly coordinated patterns of activity.
source: We observed highly modular spontaneous activity in both excitatory and inhibitory cells, with local populations showing tightly coordinated patterns of activity across cell types (Figure 6b, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by two-photon imaging data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The amplitude of events within local populations (75-µm region) was highly correlated between excitatory and inhibitory cells.
source: We found the amplitude of events within these local populations was highly correlated between excitatory and inhibitory cells (r=0.86, 2186 cells and 1231 events from 21 FOV in five animals; Figure 6c), suggesting locally balanced activity.
evidence: This is supported by local population analysis shown in Figure 6c.

claim: Both inhibitory and excitatory neurons exhibited spatially organized pairwise correlations across spontaneous events, with distributed patches of positively correlated cells located hundreds of microns away.
source: Both inhibitory and excitatory neurons exhibited spatially organized pairwise correlations across spontaneous events, with distributed patches of positively correlated cells located hundreds of microns away.
evidence: This is supported by pairwise correlation analysis at cellular resolution.

claim: The spatial structure of pairwise correlations for a given neuron (whether inhibitory or excitatory) with either inhibitory or excitatory cells was well aligned.
source: Notably, the spatial structure of pairwise correlations for a given neuron (whether inhibitory or excitatory) with either inhibitory or excitatory cells was well aligned (p<0.001 vs. shuffle), irrespective of cell type (Figure 6d, Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by pairwise correlation analysis shown in Figure 6d.

claim: Correlated excitatory and inhibitory networks exhibit a similar spatial scale at the cellular level.
source: Finally, examining correlation strength as a function of distance and cell type demonstrates that correlated excitatory and inhibitory networks exhibit a similar spatial scale at the cellular level (Figure 6e and f).
evidence: This is supported by distance-dependent correlation analysis shown in Figure 6e and f.

claim: Prior to eye-opening and the onset of reliable stimulus-evoked responses, intracortical inhibition is both present and highly organized.
source: We show that prior to eye-opening and the onset of reliable stimulus-evoked responses (Chapman et al., 1996), intracortical inhibition is both present and highly organized, with inhibitory networks already displaying patterns of modular and correlated spontaneous activity that span several millimeters.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion supported by the experimental findings.

claim: Inhibitory networks exhibit quantitatively similar structures to excitatory networks, which together show precise alignment at both local and global scales in the patterns of correlated spontaneous activity.
source: Inhibitory networks exhibit quantitatively similar structures to excitatory networks, which together show precise alignment at both local and global scales in the patterns of correlated spontaneous activity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion supported by the quantitative comparisons.

claim: In the mature ferret, both inhibitory and excitatory neurons are organized into a columnar map of orientation preference.
source: In the mature ferret, both inhibitory and excitatory neurons are organized into a columnar map of orientation preference, with orientation-specific subnetworks of functionally coupled excitatory and inhibitory neurons present not only within iso-orientation domains but also near orientation pinwheels (Wilson et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wilson et al., 2017.

claim: In rodent cortex, inhibitory neurons show non-specific local pooling of nearby excitatory activity.
source: This organization stands in contrast to the non-specific local pooling of nearby excitatory activity by inhibitory neurons found in the 'salt-and-pepper' rodent cortex (Kerlin et al., 2010; Bock et al., 2011; Hofer et al., 2011; Packer and Yuste, 2011; Runyan and Sur, 2013; Scholl et al., 2015)
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to studies of rodent cortex.

claim: The finding of sharp correlation fractures in inhibitory networks is inconsistent with non-specific local pooling.
source: However, our finding of sharp correlation fractures in inhibitory networks (Figure 3f, Figure 3—figure supplement 2) is inconsistent with non-specific local pooling and argues strongly against this possibility.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the fracture data.

claim: In the developing visual cortex, inhibitory neurons are already tightly integrated into functionally specific networks.
source: Rather, our results indicate that in the developing visual cortex, inhibitory neurons are already tightly integrated into functionally specific networks.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: The patterns of correlated activity undergo extensive refinement in the week prior to eye-opening.
source: Furthermore, given that the patterns of correlated activity undergo extensive refinement in the week prior to eye-opening (Smith et al., 2018), these results also suggest that excitatory and inhibitory networks likely refine in parallel over development to produce the tightly coupled organization found in the mature cortex (Wilson et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Smith et al., 2018.

claim: Excitatory and inhibitory networks likely refine in parallel over development to produce the tightly coupled organization found in the mature cortex.
source: Furthermore, given that the patterns of correlated activity undergo extensive refinement in the week prior to eye-opening (Smith et al., 2018), these results also suggest that excitatory and inhibitory networks likely refine in parallel over development to produce the tightly coupled organization found in the mature cortex (Wilson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the findings and prior work.

claim: The mDlx enhancer drives expression across several subtypes of inhibitory cells.
source: The mDlx enhancer used in this study has been shown to drive expression across several subtypes of inhibitory cells (Dimidschstein et al., 2016), which have been ascribed distinct roles within cortical circuits (see (Hattori et al., 2017; Wood et al., 2017) for reviews).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: In the mature ferret, parvalbumin (PV), somatostatin (SOM) and non-PV, non-SOM GABAergic neurons were all found to be equivalently integrated into specific and spatially organized functional networks.
source: However, in the mature ferret, parvalbumin (PV), somatostatin (SOM) and non-PV, non-SOM GABAergic neurons were all found to be equivalently integrated into specific and spatially organized functional networks (Wilson et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wilson et al., 2017.

claim: Large-scale distributed functional networks are a hallmark of mature cortical organization and are exemplified by the columnar arrangement of orientation preference in the visual cortex of primates and carnivores.
source: Large-scale distributed functional networks are a hallmark of mature cortical organization and are exemplified by the columnar arrangement of orientation preference in the visual cortex of primates and carnivores (Blasdel and Salama, 1986; Bonhoeffer and Grinvald, 1991; Ohki et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to studies of mature cortex.

claim: Co-tuned columns are preferentially interconnected by specific long-range horizontal projections.
source: Here, co-tuned columns preferentially interconnected by specific long-range horizontal projections (Gilbert and Wiesel, 1989; Malach et al., 1993; Bosking et al., 1997) which emerge over the course of development (Ruthazer and Stryker, 1996; Borrell and Callaway, 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to studies of cortical connectivity.

claim: Long-range horizontal projections emerge over the course of development.
source: Here, co-tuned columns preferentially interconnected by specific long-range horizontal projections (Gilbert and Wiesel, 1989; Malach et al., 1993; Bosking et al., 1997) which emerge over the course of development (Ruthazer and Stryker, 1996; Borrell and Callaway, 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to developmental studies.

claim: The presence of modular activity and long range-correlations in the developing cortex prior to the emergence of horizontal connections, coupled with the finding that correlations persist in the absence of feedforward input, indicates that local intracortical circuits are sufficient to generate these patterns of activity.
source: The presence of modular activity and long range-correlations in the developing cortex prior to the emergence of these horizontal connections, coupled with the finding that correlations persist in the absence of feedforward input (Smith et al., 2018), has been taken to indicate that local intracortical circuits are sufficient to generate these patterns of activity.
evidence: This is an inference based on prior findings and the current results.

claim: Models of developing cortical networks can rely on local connectivity to self-organize, thereby producing modular patterns of activity.
source: Models of developing cortical networks can rely on local connectivity to self-organize, thereby producing modular patterns of activity (von der Malsburg, 1973; Swindale, 1997; Miller, 1994; Barrow et al., 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to computational models.

claim: If local connections are sufficiently heterogeneous, the resulting patterns of activity reside in a low-dimensional subspace and produce long-range correlations without requiring long-range horizontal connections.
source: If these local connections are sufficiently heterogeneous, the resulting patterns of activity reside in a low-dimensional subspace and produce long-range correlations without requiring long-range horizontal connections (Smith et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Smith et al., 2018.

claim: A strong prediction of locally heterogeneous network models is the presence of tightly integrated and co-aligned excitatory and inhibitory networks.
source: A strong prediction of such models is the presence of tightly integrated and co-aligned excitatory and inhibitory networks (Ermentrout and Cowan, 1979; Wilson and Cowan, 1973), in agreement with our experimental observations in the developing cortex.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to theoretical models.

claim: Short-range intracortical interactions between tightly coupled excitatory and inhibitory circuits give rise to large-scale distributed networks during early development.
source: Thus, our results suggest that short-range intracortical interactions between tightly coupled excitatory and inhibitory circuits give rise to large-scale distributed networks during early development, which may serve as a seed for future functional organization in the cortex.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the findings and theoretical considerations.

claim: Large-scale distributed networks during early development may serve as a seed for future functional organization in the cortex.
source: Thus, our results suggest that short-range intracortical interactions between tightly coupled excitatory and inhibitory circuits give rise to large-scale distributed networks during early development, which may serve as a seed for future functional organization in the cortex.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion about the developmental role of early networks.

claim: Viral injections targeted the primary visual cortex, defined as thalamo-recipient visual cortex.
source: Injections targeted the primary visual cortex, defined as thalamo-recepient visual cortex.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology.

claim: In the ferret, primary visual cortex includes both areas 17 and 18, which both receive direct thalamic innervation and exhibit columnar mapping of orientation.
source: In the ferret, primary visual cortex includes both areas 17 and 18, which both receive direct thalamic innervation and exhibit columnar mapping of orientation (White et al., 1999; White et al., 2001a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to anatomical studies.

claim: Eye-opening in ferret typically occurs between P31 and P34.
source: Widefield imaging of spontaneous activity in the primary visual cortex was performed at postnatal days 23–29 (P23–29, n=7 animals), approximately 7 days before eye-opening (typically between P31 and P34)
evidence: This is a factual statement about ferret development.

claim: Both inhibitory and excitatory networks show highly similar Large versus All correlation similarities, though excitatory similarities are greater than inhibitory.
source: Both inhibitory and excitatory networks show highly similar Large versus All correlation similarities, though excitatory similarities are greater than inhibitory (I: 0.87 [0.80–0.90], n=7. E: 0.98 [0.97–0.98],n=7, p=0.0088, Wilcoxon rank-sum test).
evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1f.
